title: Hint when an item is filed unscored
lead: `add` and `import` accept an item at the default importance 2, urgency 2 and no effort without comment, so an unscored item is only noticed later when the queue does not sort.
findings_note: S139 decision: guidance only for 1.0.0, tool nudge later

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: S139 changed the agent guidance to score every filed item, and the owner chose to keep 1.0.0 to guidance and file the tool side separately. A non-blocking hint at filing time would catch unscored items from any author, not only agents that read `ai instructions`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_add`, `cmd_import`) and the import report in `src/slicer/ops.py`
- `docs/agents.md`, `README.md`
- tests for `add` and `import`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `add` of an item left at 2/2 with no effort prints a stderr hint naming `--importance`, `--urgency` and `--effort`; the exit code and JSON payload are unchanged.
2. `import --dry-run` lists unscored items in its `warnings`.
3. A scored item produces no hint.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Settle with the project before building, do not infer: whether "unscored" means 2/2 with no effort or any of the three left at its default, whether a config switch turns the hint off, and whether it belongs in `add`, `import`, or both.

Settled with the owner (2026-09-29, the agent's recommendations accepted):

- "Unscored" means all three at their defaults: importance 2, urgency 2, and no effort. A deliberate 2/2 with an effort estimate stays quiet.
- No config switch: the hint never touches stdout, the JSON payload, or the exit code.
- Both: `add` prints a stderr hint; `import` (dry run and real) lists unscored items in its existing `warnings`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The tests above pass; the suite and `slicer check` pass.
